_comment: Justified exceptions to the console-url hygiene gate (#75 / S4).
The gate exists because a PLAYBACK or API url carries `ApiKey=<the session access token>`.
An exception is only defensible when the value can never be one of those. Two classes
qualify today, and each entry below says which one it is and why:
server-address — an ORIGIN the user typed or the server advertised (`http://host:8096`).
No path, no query string, therefore no credential. These are the
connection-diagnostic lines, and an address is the only thing that
makes a failed connection diagnosable at all.
app-route      — an in-app route the router was asked to show. It never leaves the
client and is never authenticated; it carries item ids at worst.
Anything that is or may become a media url, a `/Videos`, `/Audio` or api url, or any url
built by `playbackmanager`, does NOT qualify. Log an endpoint category instead
An entry that stops matching fails the gate, so this file cannot rot into a blanket
permission. `expression` is matched on the argument's source text, whitespace-collapsed.

exceptions.reason: `url` is a server origin from the connection candidate list; the request built from it appends `/System/Info/Public` and is unauthenticated. Which candidate was tried is the diagnosis.
Same origin value as the line above, on the success branch. No credential is reachable from it.
Same origin value as the line above, on the failure branch. Which address failed is the only useful thing to say here.
`urls` is built two lines up as `http://${address}` — an origin and nothing else.
The server-address candidate list, printed before each is probed at `/System/Info/Public`. Origins only, no query string.
The in-app route `appRouter.show` rejected. It is client-side, unauthenticated, and never a media or api url.
